primary_hypothesis: H1: A history-conditioned transformer RL2 policy trained only on action_scale and action_noise achieves a positive context-matched adaptation gap on unseen action_latency: G_i = mean_return_adaptive_i - mean_return_history_blocked_i > 0 across independent training seeds i. Adaptive and history-blocked evaluations use identical weights, current augmented observations, context lengths, positional indices, episode seeds, and fault draws; only access to prior tokens by the final query is removed.
secondary_question: Does the adaptive sequence policy provide better held-out control performance than an independently trained single-token reactive REDQ baseline receiving the same augmented observation token?

primary_ablation.name: history_blocked_context_matched
primary_ablation.definition: Preserve the adaptive context deque, sequence length, current augmented token, and positional index, but block the final transformer query from attending to prior tokens in every transformer block.

secondary_ablation.name: context_reset
secondary_ablation.definition: Clear the context deque before every action. This is retained as a secondary diagnostic only because it also changes the sequence-length regime.

validation_faults.notes: Validation uses only training fault mechanisms with unseen parameter ranges. The same validation episode seeds are reused for every checkpoint comparison. Test faults are never used for checkpoint selection.

predetermined_decision_rules.CASE_A: mean G > 0 and 95% seed-level bootstrap CI excludes 0 on positive side -> SUPPORTED POSITIVE CONTEXT-MATCHED ADAPTATION
predetermined_decision_rules.CASE_B: 95% seed-level bootstrap CI includes 0 -> ADAPTATION NOT ESTABLISHED
predetermined_decision_rules.CASE_C: mean G < 0 and 95% seed-level bootstrap CI excludes 0 on negative side -> NEGATIVE HISTORY EFFECT
predetermined_decision_rules.CASE_D: large heterogeneous seed effects with inconsistent signs across seeds -> SEED-SENSITIVE / UNSTABLE
